clips.title: The story
paras: Near the Den, Vile Familiars threaten every warlock who seeks the power of demons. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength against them and bring back their heads. This is the humble, dangerous first step toward mastering fel power under the Horde’s watchful eyes.

Warlocks live uneasily within Thrall’s new Horde. Demonic corruption and blood pacts once brought ruin to the orcs, leaving deep scars and distrust. Fel magic is tolerated in Durotar, but its practitioners are neither loved nor welcomed. Many warlocks live in seclusion, practicing in shadowed places like the Den, away from prying eyes. There, they teach the few initiates daring enough to follow their path.

Ruzan asks you to prove your strength before he teaches you the dangerous rites for bending an imp to your will. Vile Familiars skulk near a cave northeast of the Den and hurl bolts of flame at those who approach. Slay these lesser demons and bring back their heads to show you can overcome the fiery creatures you hope to control. Only then can you face the danger of the magic you seek to command.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Those warlocks who came before us have earned the distrust of the Horde, and while we are tolerated, we are not loved.

This has not brought the warlocks closer together, however, as many choose to live reclusively, dabbling in their magics alone. I will not seek to lead you down one path or the other, but only help you in your maturation.
Before I teach you the art of summoning, bring me six heads of the vile familiars from the cave to the northeast.

clips.title: Progress
paras: It is important that you can control the beings that you summon through your magic. There are few enough interested in learning the ways of the adventurer that I would risk throwing your life away by teaching you something before you are ready.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Throughout your training as an adventurer, you will learn to call forth beings of many sorts. Some may not seem it, but all are useful tools.
Do not be fooled by the imp's small size. As you no doubt noticed, it is still a formidable adversary.
